## How to check this yourself

Each command reads public data and changes nothing. Use the full commit above.

```sh
gh release view v3.48.10 --repo mario-andreschak/FLUJO
npm view flujo-ai@3.48.10 dist
npm audit signatures   # inside a project that installed flujo-ai@3.48.10
gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/mario-andreschak/flujo:3.48.10 --repo mario-andreschak/FLUJO --signer-workflow mario-andreschak/FLUJO/.github/workflows/publish-image.yml --source-digest 174ffaf034532b1ec52e483724563309e1fc9693 --deny-self-hosted-runners
gh release download v3.48.10 --repo mario-andreschak/FLUJO --pattern flujo-setup.exe
gh attestation verify flujo-setup.exe --repo mario-andreschak/FLUJO --signer-workflow mario-andreschak/FLUJO/.github/workflows/installer.yml --source-digest 174ffaf034532b1ec52e483724563309e1fc9693 --deny-self-hosted-runners
npm pack flujo-ai@3.48.10
gh attestation verify flujo-ai-3.48.10.tgz --repo mario-andreschak/FLUJO --signer-workflow mario-andreschak/FLUJO/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml --source-digest 174ffaf034532b1ec52e483724563309e1fc9693 --deny-self-hosted-runners
```

On Windows, `Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\flujo-setup.exe` shows whether the installer is code-signed.
The full steps are in [release distribution verification](../../release-distribution-verification.md).

## What this page does not prove

- It reads the signed build records from GitHub's and npm's stores and checks the
  commit, workflow and file hashes they name. It does not check the cryptographic
  signatures themselves; the commands above do.
- CI and test results are for the source on the release commit. Installing and
  using the npm package, the image or the installer is a separate check (#570, #572).
- It says nothing about real users, long real-model runs, or human use (#577, and
  the targets in the [scorecard foundation contract](../scorecard-foundation.md)).
- Alert counts need a GitHub login with access to the repository's security alerts.
